svg.text: every vector Xθ lives in this plane
the best a linear model can do
Read it row by row: the residual is orthogonal to every column of X.
Least squares is not an algebraic trick — it is a projection onto col(X).
If two columns are collinear the plane collapses to a line: the projection still exists,
but θ̂ is no longer unique — which is exactly when XᵀX stops being invertible.
